items: What is approved here is a profile and a set of signing responsibilities, not a headcount table.

source: Source: IC Memo v2 §7.8, §7.9; capability-model working table §7.2; candidate CVs (2026-11-01); data as of 2026-10-13
notes: We judge people by the decisions they are accountable for, not by titles. Two layers are covered by named candidates; the science and product lead is the hire that unblocks everything else, because that layer adjudicates the patient-cell and platform-transfer gates and rules on whether a read-out qualifies at the other four. Services such as patient-derived cells, functional assays, animal work and toxicology can be bought in, but interpretation and attribution of failure stay inside the company. Cut for space: the full decision-rights matrix across the five decision types, and the adviser-support arrangements that bridge the period before formal appointment.

regions.text: Authorisation stops at the receptor-entry and patient-cell gates. Every gate has three preset fallbacks - rework, downgrade the claim, or partner - and the IC chooses; no tranche auto-releases.

notes: Order is set by dependency, not by a calendar. The freedom-to-operate and backbone work and the conjugate characterization work start in parallel with the productive-delivery study; the second-payload and in vivo studies are strictly downstream. Two evidence gaps remain open - intact molecule in blood, and effective intracellular payload - and only the second falls inside this round's scope. Across thirteen reference programmes including one control, none has direct in-material data on effective intracellular payload: that is a gap, not a proven rate-limiting step. Each fallback carries a cash limit, and a miss is decided by the IC among four options rather than releasing the next tranche.

source: Source: IC Memo v2 §4.5 (patent snapshot; no freedom-to-operate conclusion), Appendix B; route comparison table; patent search set as of 2026-09-07; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: Work around rights at the antibody and backbone layers, not by switching tissue: changing tissue costs biology, changing antibody costs data. Two further options sit on the same axes without being acquisition routes - buy a short evaluation or an option first and decide afterwards, or hold and watch with written re-entry triggers. This round reaches no freedom-to-operate conclusion: a scanning-stage search does not support a non-infringement view, and changing epitope or sequence is not by itself a design-around. The backbone-chemistry layer returned no patent family numbers, which means the search scope is not yet defined, not that the layer is free; if two separately named chemistries prove identical, that layer immediately becomes named and licensable only. Cut for space: the item-by-item table of what each alternative design releases and what it costs.

regions.text: The two cases diverge on one point: which read-out the first experiment buys. Amounts follow the four prerequisites and like-for-like quotes; RMB 47m is a muscle-construct scenario only.

source: Source: IC Memo v2 §4.3, §7.2, §7.3, §7.7, §7.9; budget quantity-driver schedule; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: What goes to the IC is a line-item structure tied to gates, not a total. A budget can only be built after company positioning, the case for AOC, the patient and target product profile, and the availability of technology rights are settled; setting a raise first and back-filling the pipeline turns gate criteria into reporting decoration. The conservative case buys discrimination fastest - the productive-delivery study is the only one that can start without a fixed disease direction, and the most valuable result is similar uptake with more than fivefold difference in functional potency. The aggressive case goes straight at the functional endpoint and exposes failure one notch slower. The three construct families bottleneck on different resources: muscle nuclear repair on donor myotubes and two functional assays, with diaphragm samples unobtainable in vitro and needing planning early; fibroblast delivery on clinical sampling, which is feasible; kidney-cell entry on scarce models, where not verified is not the same as non-existent. Public data do not support generic unit-cost figures, and cost per effective course is an output of the CMC and cost gate, not an input here.

title: Financing, dilution and exit on one basis; three cash-flow types modelled separately with parameters still to fill

regions.heading: Three cash flows, modelled separately and never netted

items.heading: Equity return
items.body: Paid at exit by holding and preference order. Exit value is set by the whole company, which licence income influences but does not equal; 'stake x equity value' holds only with single-class common. Amount TBD.

items.heading: Company licence income
items.body: Upfront, milestones and royalties accrue to the company, with the development obligations. It raises company value and so equity return indirectly, but counting it as shareholder recovery double-counts. Terms TBD.

items.heading: Related-party service income
items.body: Group-side revenue from NewCo buying services from the group: a NewCo cost, opposite to equity return and not an investment return. Turning capital into related-party purchasing does not remove risk. Pricing TBD.

source: Source: Governance and terms basis 04 §1.2, §2.1-§2.3 (shareholders, roles and protective provisions TBD); IC Memo v2; team analysis
notes: We are submitting two empty tables with their rules and a list of parameters to fill, not numbers. The three cash flows must stay separate because merging them either double-counts or hides an obligation. We do not reuse comparable-transaction return figures: different entry risk, different rights position and different capital structure make those multiples uninformative here. Governance terms already agreed in principle: no controlling stake, no board majority, a customer-data firewall accepted by both quality organisations, and no exclusive-sourcing requirement. Tranche structure is already determined by the gates, so financing instalments follow gate read-outs rather than a calendar.

regions.text: Only counsel's written directional opinion is a release condition; the full rights opinion and targeted freedom-to-operate work are standalone diligence deliverables, not funding switches.

source: Source: IC Memo v2 §7.2, §7.3, §7.7, §7.8; stop-condition annex to the investment agreement; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: A rights conclusion is a switch on scope of work, not a switch on money. Three downside cases are pre-scripted with immediate actions and an inventory list: the asset reduces to a single product, rights are not obtained, or a key person does not take up post. Five consideration groups are kept separate, share no parameters, and are all TBD. One sequencing conflict must be resolved before the terms are finalised: the targeted freedom-to-operate work is placed before the receptor-entry gate in one source and after the construct is fixed in another, and under our own definition the construct is fixed only after that gate reads out, so the two cannot both stand. The criteria behind each stop are two-sided where the source is two-sided: at the patient-cell gate, the target must change and function must recover in patient cells while normal cells are not over-affected.

regions.heading: What the IC is asked to settle
items: Nine resolutions voted item by item and six open slots filled; authorisation stops at a defined preparation and verification period, after which the IC decides again.
Conversations run in two stages, and the first stage can stand even if the second lapses.
Two candidates, conflicts of interest not yet cleared: no in-depth discussion, no terms, no equity and no title until that gate closes.
No question asks for a former employer's confidential material; any question touching undisclosed current-employer content is stopped on the spot.

source: Source: Candidate discussion outline 2026-10-20 §0, §2, §4-§5; IC Memo v2 §4.2.2; Cochran et al., J Med Chem 2026;69(17):20230-20247
notes: Questions are ordered by discriminating power, and each one is written to land on a single decision rather than on an impression. Avoid open questions about what the candidate finds exciting: they produce agreement, not information. For each question we also fix what source material we want to see - published methods, publicly discussable cases, the candidate's own reasoning - so that nothing asked requires a former employer's confidential information. Cut for space: the governance questions, the single most important question of the session, and the detail of the six open slots.
